newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia Banco de Bogota raises dividend.
newsitem.headline: Colombia Banco de Bogota raises dividend.

text.p: Colombia's Banco de Bogota is to raise its dividend by 24.59 percent to 38 pesos per share per month from April through September, the securities superintendency said Thursday.

The dividend was raised from its previous level of 30.5 pesos per share after the bank, Colombia's fourth largest in terms of assets, posted a 60.2 percent upturn in net profits in 1996 -- 122 billion pesos.
The decision means that a total 38.06 billion pesos will be paid in dividends across 166.9 fully paid up shares to Dec. 31, the securities superintendency said.

The superintendency, the stock exchange watchdog, said the bank had also announced its intention to go ahead with a rights issue expected to raise an additional 21.04 billion pesos. Shares will be offered at a ratio of one for every existing 50 shares at a price of 6,300 pesos. Banco de Bogota closed at 6,490 each Thursday.

In announcing its decision, Banco de Bogota said it would be holding back 43.17 billion pesos as a reserve fund. A Bogota stock broker, who did not wish to be named, said the fund was "almost certainly" to finance plans to fend off imminent competiton in Colombia from Spanish banks.

Banco Bilbao-Vizcaya bought a 40 percent stake and took administrative control of Banco Ganadero, Colombia's largest bank in terms of assets, last year. Banco Santander and Banco Central Hispano are set to launch into the Colombian market sometime this year.
"That reserve fund will be used to expand its branches or possibly to merge with another institution in the face of Spanish competition," the broker said.
